request.state: CanTime records Employee-owned Entry rows with project and frozen rate. The current correct scenario is by=project_manager; it checks can_work(actor,entry.project.location), state in [rejected,approved,exported], from<until and a nonblank reason, then creates a replacement and Correction without invalidating the original overlap or billing source. Its bill scenario is by=project_manager and requires location authority, approved state, billable, nonnull customer and positive amount. Canonical invoice BillingV1 has charge(value:Charge)->OperationOutcome, cancel(source:text,reason:text)->OperationOutcome, refund(source:text,amount:money,reason:text)->OperationOutcome, reconcile(source:text)->Settlement? and event settled {value:Settlement}. Settlement includes source, invoice, revision, amount, collected, refunded, collection_pending, refund_pending, state and recorded_at. Invoice cancellation installs a permanent source fence, disables collection, yields released only with void and no outstanding collected money, and reports unavailable when money was collected; refunds cannot proceed while attempts are pending/unknown and may require finance for external/split payments. Remote receipts do not prove billing settlement. All alternatives must retain old evidence, record manager actor/reason, suppress replacement export until its original financial obligation is safely resolved, use one local D1 owner transaction, and keep imports explicitly proposed. PeriodReview will snapshot Employee-owned completed draft entries wholly within from/until, atomically submit all, approve all only after current manager grants, and return rejected/withdrawn entries to draft with recorded decision. Half-open overlaps must be checked for timers, manual intake, edits and corrections; only project managers can supply an attributed exception. These are draft source/JS changes, not runtime implementation.

time_correction.instructions: Select the approach that best preserves monetary correctness, review evidence and manageable source complexity under the stated contracts; treat this as design advice, not execution proof.

criteria.A: Cancel the entire original source, reconcile cumulative settlement, explicitly refund its remaining collected funds and reconcile again; a fresh replacement source can bill only after no pending collection/refund, zero net collected money and confirmed source release. This handles upward and downward corrections uniformly but can refund and recollect money and require finance intervention.
criteria.B: Keep the original invoice, compare replacement money with its frozen amount and send only a separate positive charge or partial refund, reconciling each delta before marking the correction complete. This avoids full refund/recollection but requires cumulative adjustment tracking, safe allocation across successive revisions, and separate overlap/source bookkeeping.
